small_guidance:
- The stats kernel uses atomic_add across many M-tiles per column; replace with a two-stage reduction (per-block partial sums written to a [num_m_blocks, N] buffer, then a small reduce kernel) or use larger BLOCK_M (e.g. 1024-2048) to cut the number of atomics by 2-4×.
- Autotune both kernels over (BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, num_warps, num_stages): try 128×256/8w/3s, 256×128/8w/3s, 64×256/4w/4s for the apply kernel; the current 128×128/8w is likely suboptimal for 16384×4096.
- Fuse the addmm into the same kernel as the scale+stats by writing a tiled GEMM that produces y, multiplies by scale, and accumulates column sum/sumsq in the epilogue — this removes the separate y materialization read/write (M*N=64M floats = 256MB traffic).
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as a single fused tiled GEMM (`tl.dot`, BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=32, GROUP_M=8) that computes `y = x @ W.t() + b`, multiplies by `scale` in the epilogue, and atomically accumulates per-column sum and sumsq into N-sized buffers — eliminating the intermediate y read in the stats pass.
- Keep y resident by making the GEMM persistent per N-tile column-strip: each program iterates over all M-tiles of a fixed N-tile, accumulates stats locally (no atomics across M), writes y, then a tiny second kernel finalizes mean/invstd; a third kernel applies the affine. This trades one full read of y for in-register reduction.
- Alternatively, since the apply pass needs (mean, invstd) which depend on the full M reduction, structure as: (1) fused GEMM+scale+per-column partial reduction into [num_pid_m, N] buffer, (2) reduce-and-finalize kernel computing a,b of size N, (3) fused apply that reads y once and writes out — total y traffic is 1R+1W instead of current 2R+2W.
